references.text: God promises Abraham that the covenant will be confirmed with Isaac, not Ishmael. This is the basis for God now telling Abraham to listen to Sarah.
God calls Isaac Abraham's 'only son,' confirming that lineage is reckoned through him.
Paul quotes this verse and explains that it is not the children of the flesh who are God's children, but the children of the promise who are counted as offspring.
Hebrews directly quotes 'In Isaac shall your offspring be named' as an example of Abraham's faith.
Paul uses the allegory of Sarah and Hagar to show that the children of the promise (through Isaac) are the true heirs, quoting Sarah's demand to cast out the slave woman.
21:12 confirms and reinforces the prophecy about Isaac as heir from 17:19.
Highlights Sarah's role: obedience to her husband (1 Pet) versus authority in God's plan (Gen 21).
Contrast: Earlier Abraham listened to Sarah's human advice (16:2); now he must listen to God's plan through her (21:12).
Isaiah confirms that God's promise to Abraham was fulfilled through Sarah, as explained in 21:12.
21:12 provides the theological basis for the naming action in 21:3.
21:12 is the resolution to the conflict between Sarah and Hagar that began in 16:5.
21:12 gives concrete content to 'offspring' in the covenant mentioned in Acts 3:25.
21:12 provides the theological basis for the event in 21:2.
Direct quote or allusion emphasizing that only Isaac's line is God's people.
